message.content:
When it comes to jazz vocalists, “best” is always a matter of taste and context, but a few names consistently rise to the top of most lists:

| Singer | Why they’re often called the best |
|--------|-----------------------------------|
| **Ella Fitzgerald** | Known as the “First Lady of Song,” her impeccable pitch, scat‑sing mastery, and effortless phrasing set a gold standard for jazz vocals. |
| **Billie Holiday** | Her deeply emotive delivery and unique phrasing turned standards into personal statements; she’s a benchmark for emotional depth in jazz singing. |
| **Louis Armstrong** (vocalist) | Though famed as a trumpeter, his gravelly voice and charismatic stage presence made him one of the first true jazz pop stars. |
| **Frank Sinatra** | His smooth baritone and impeccable timing made him a crossover icon, bridging jazz, pop, and big‑band styles. |
| **Nat King Cole** | A blend of jazz, blues, and pop, his warm baritone and lyrical phrasing earned him the nickname “The King of Swing.” |

If you’re looking for a single “best” singer, many jazz aficionados point to **Ella Fitzgerald** for her technical brilliance and timeless influence. However, the beauty of jazz is that each vocalist brings a distinct voice and style—so the “best” can vary depending on what you value most: technical skill, emotional depth, or crossover appeal.
